book_title: Mukhtasar al-Athar: The Summary of the Narrations

chapters.title: The First Obligation: Seeking Knowledge
chapters.rationale: The opening seam is the merit and etiquette of seeking knowledge, from the verses exalting the learned through Ja'far al-Sadiq's warning that the believer inherits either knowledge and refinement or ignorance and bad character.

chapters.title: Purity: Water, Ablution, and the Body Made Ready
chapters.rationale: A single coherent domain of taharah, seamed from the merits of purity and the purity of water through ablution, ghusl, clean garments, the siwak, tayammum, and the rules of menstruation.

chapters.title: The Pillar of Religion: Standing in Prayer
chapters.rationale: The core act of salah as a lived practice — its merit and appointed times, the call, the mosque, the imamate, the ranks, and the full bodily form from opening takbir to the final salam.

chapters.title: Supplication and the Many Forms of Prayer
chapters.rationale: Everything surrounding the daily rite: the tashahhud and the culture of supplication, what speech and action are permitted within prayer, dress, and the situational prayers — Friday, the two Eids, omissions, interruptions, the latecomer, children, travelers, the sick, fear, eclipse, drought, witr, the reckoning of obligatory and voluntary units, and prostration at the verses of the Qur'an.

chapters.title: Facing Death: The Rites of the Departed
chapters.rationale: The Book of Funerals as one arc, seamed from visiting the sick and the meaning of death through washing, shrouding and embalming, the funeral procession and prayer, and burial in the grave.

chapters.title: The Due of Wealth: Zakat
chapters.rationale: The Book of Zakat entire — the command and its severity, payment to the rightful Imams, the thresholds for gold and silver, livestock, the conduct of collectors, grains and fruits, and Zakat al-Fitr, closing the first part of the work.

chapters.title: The Fast: Ramadan and the Discipline of Abstention
chapters.rationale: The Book of Fasting as a unit — its merit and how the fast begins and is broken, dispensations for travel and illness, the Night of Power, the taxonomy of obligatory and voluntary fasts, and i'tikaf.

chapters.title: The Journey to the House: Pilgrimage
chapters.rationale: The whole Book of Hajj held together as one long journey — its obligation and preparation, the visit to the Prophet's city, the miqats and ihram, hunting penalties, the Haram, tawaf and sa'i, tamattu', Arafah, Muzdalifah, the stoning, the offering, the shaving, the acts and departure of Mina, standalone umrah, prevention and siege, pilgrimage on another's behalf, missed hajj, and the vow.

chapters.title: The Sword and the State: Jihad, Governance, and Justice
chapters.rationale: The concluding Book of Jihad and statecraft — the obligation and virtue of struggle, the duties of commanders and princes, the call to Islam, the conduct of battle, the treatment of captives and the granting of security, reconciliation and jizya, the division of spoils, the fighting of rebels, and those among the people of the Qibla — deniers, brigands, apostates, and heretics — who must be confronted.
